name: Silk
rationale: Clean-room WebGL port written from the one-line effect description only (no upstream source read): a dependency-free fragment shader gives hero panels and cards a quiet, slowly flowing fabric texture that is safe under text, with a static CSS gradient when WebGL is unavailable.

color.description: Fabric colour, as #rgb or #rrggbb; also tints the CSS fallback gradient.

speed.description: Flow speed; 0 holds a still frame.

scale.description: Fold density; larger gives more, narrower folds.

rotation.description: Direction of the folds, in degrees.

noise.description: Film-grain amount, which also hides gradient banding.

a11y: The injected canvas is aria-hidden and pointer-events: none; the host's content, reading order and focus behaviour are unchanged.
The texture is deliberately low-contrast, but its highlights are light, so text on it should carry a shadow or scrim to keep 4.5:1 contrast (the demo does this).
Reduced motion stops the shader loop and the fallback drift and shows one still frame of the fabric.
Forced-colors mode hides the canvas and paints the host in Canvas/CanvasText with a visible border.
